Fetch environmental-assessment records from Georgia.

Source: R/get_assessments_ge.R
get_assessments_ge.Rd

Implementation of get_assessments() for Georgia. Backed by the recent environmental decision portal of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture (https://ei.gov.ge/, Georgian-language /ka pages). The legacy archive is out of scope, and the portal's own historical horizon is not documented (cases from 2024-08 onward were observed): only what the listing returns is covered, so results are not national completeness. Native Georgian values are kept verbatim.

Usage

get_assessments_ge(
  date_range = NULL,
  limit = Inf,
  download = FALSE,
  cache_dir = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  max_file_size_mb = NULL,
  write_sidecar = TRUE,
  refresh = FALSE,
  topic = NULL,
  relevance_threshold = NULL,
  relevance_model = NULL,
  procedure = NULL,
  query = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

date_range, limit, download, cache_dir, overwrite, max_file_size_mb, write_sidecar, refresh, topic, relevance_threshold, relevance_model

See get_assessments().

procedure

Optional character vector of procedure keys (see Procedures); NULL (default) enumerates all six.

query

Optional free-text query, matched client-side as a case-insensitive substring of the record title.

...

Reserved for future extensions; unused arguments are warned about.

Value

A tibble; see get_assessments() for the required schema.

Records

The listing (POST /ka/Home/Table, anonymous JSON body, 5 rows per page, a finite page count) holds procedure events; the stable case key is the /ka/info/<GUID> link. One output record is returned per case (deduplicated across pages and procedures) with document_id = "ge_<GUID>". The case detail JSON (GET /ka/record?id=<GUID>) is captured in full in detail_json; title (project name), proponent (implementer), jurisdiction (activity address, free text "region/municipality"), date_published (earliest procedure publication date, else the listing date), status / status_date (of the procedure that surfaced the case; a listing row that is a nested-document event is resolved to its enclosing procedure, and an unmatched row falls back to the listing-row cells), procedure_native, category_native and procedures_native (all procedures of the case) are columns. competent_authority is not exposed (NA). The cells of the listing row that surfaced the case are kept as listing_row_id, listing_municipality, listing_comment_deadline and listing_public_hearing; later event rows of the same case are not merged. An empty procedure grid is an error (planscanR_error_bad_response); no sidecar is written, so the case is retried on the next run. assessment_type comes from the procedure filter that found the case ("EIA" or "SEA"); no title heuristic is used.

Procedures

procedure selects which procedure types to enumerate: "eia", "eia_screening", "eia_scoping", "sea_screening", "sea_scoping", "sea_report_review". The default is all six; exemption and permit-change procedures are not covered.

Attachments

Files are listed from the detail JSON for every procedure and nested document, never guessed: attachment_urls_main_document holds /download/files/?file=<GUID>&accompany=false PDFs (application letters, decisions) where HasDocument is true; attachment_urls_accompanying_bundle holds accompany=true downloads only where the record says HasAccompanyingDocument. The EIA report itself lives inside the RAR5 accompanying bundle. Bundles are downloaded as-is (no extraction, no new dependency). Where the report is: the EIA report sits in the accompanying bundle of the EIA procedure's application/annex entry (for SEA, of the report-review procedure); screening and scoping bundles hold screening and scoping material only. Accompanying files can also be PDFs, not only RAR. SEA report-review bundles are often 500+ MB and some EIA bundles are over the default 50 MB cap too (e.g. a 75 MB gas-pipeline bundle); both are skipped_size. attachment_labels_native is a JSON object mapping each URL to "<native procedure name> | <native category name>".

Filter coverage

procedure is applied server-side. query (case-insensitive title substring) and date_range (against date_published) are client-side, so a selective filter still pages through the listing. Requests are throttled to 2 req/s (getOption("planscanR.ge_throttle_rate")). Page failures or empty pages give a planscanR_warning_partial; a response without the expected table is an error.

See also

get_assessments(), get_assessments_coverage().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
get_assessments_ge(limit = 3, download = FALSE, procedure = "eia")
} # }
